objective: Standard statement: (1) every planar cubic bipartite graph has at least six square faces, and exactly five faces meet a square face; (2) Theorem: every plain planar page (a planar cubic brace with a junction square face and no signs) is twisted, because a square face away from the junction has odd Kasteleyn parity; (3) Corollary: in a plain cubic Pfaffian brace every trisum square has three twisted branches, so the polynomial mechanism of TWIST-COUNT A never reaches a plain non-planar brace; (4) Corollary: the Heawood graph is the only cubic bipartite brace whose plain system is not 2-colourable, i.e. the Fano plane is the only non-2-colourable 3-regular 3-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a brace. Checks: the face test against the cut and tensor tests on every page of a family of planar braces; plain trisum braces with three twisted branches at every square; the census of non-2-colourable systems (only the Fano plane is a brace). Nearest known result: Euler's formula (classical); the Robertson-Seymour-Thomas structure theorem (splices of Fano planes) likely implies (4).
status: Proved: every plain planar page is twisted (Euler forces a square face away from the junction, where a Pfaffian signing needs an odd sign), so plain trisum braces have three twisted branches at every square; the Heawood graph (Fano) is the only brace whose plain system is not 2-colourable (likely known via RST).
title: Plain pages are always twisted
